deities: Goddess Mahalakshmi (Ambabai), presiding deity - black stone idol about 3 feet tall weighing about 40 kg, four-armed holding a mahalunga fruit, mace, shield and panpatra bowl; crowned, with a stone lion (her vahana) behind; uniquely faces west
Shri Yantra carved on one of the inner sanctum walls
Navagrahas, Surya, Mahishasuramardini, Vitthal-Rukmini, Shiva, Vishnu and Bhavani (courtyard shrines)
Visweshwar Mahadev (shrine by the Manikarnika Kund temple tank)
festivals: Navratra Mahotsav (September-October; nine days, with Lalita Panchami, Ashtami and Navami as highlights)

Kirnotsav (Sun festival, twice a year; rays of the setting sun fall on the feet, chest and face of the idol over three consecutive days - verify months, sources variously list March/September and January-February/November)

history.dynasty: Chalukya (founder traditionally Karnadeva); later patronage from the Shilaharas, Yadavas of Devagiri and the Marathas (Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj and Chhatrapati Sambhaji Maharaj); managed today by the Paschim Maharashtra Devasthan Samiti
history.summary: The Mahalaxmi Temple at Kolhapur, dedicated to Goddess Mahalakshmi worshipped as Ambabai, is one of the 108 Maha Shakti Peethas (one of the three-and-a-half Shakti Peethas of Maharashtra) and among the most revered shrines of the Shakta tradition. Legend holds that the goddess slew the demon Kolhasur here at Karavira, and the city takes its name from him. The temple was built in the 7th century CE by the Chalukya king Karnadeva and expanded over the centuries by the Shilaharas, Yadavas and Marathas; its architecture blends Chalukya, Hemadpanti, Dravida and Maratha styles, with the black-stone sanctum and shikhara as the oldest core. The about 3-foot, 40-kg idol faces west (unusual among Hindu temples) and is four-armed, holding a mahalunga fruit, mace, shield and drinking bowl, with a lion behind it and a Shri Yantra carved on a sanctum wall. Twice a year the setting sun's rays fall directly on the idol (Kirnotsav). Note: based on a 12th-century Kannada text, some historians claim the shrine began as a Jain temple dedicated to Chandraprabh Tirthankar and was later converted - this is a scholarly claim, not the received tradition. It is customary for devotees to visit Tirumala, Kolhapur Mahalakshmi and Tiruchanur Padmavathi as a single yatra.

name: Mahalaxmi Temple
town_description: Kolhapur, on the banks of the Panchaganga river in south-western Maharashtra, is one of the state's great historic cities and a former princely state capital under the Bhosales. It is known for the Panhala Fort, the New Palace museum, Rankala Lake, Kushti wrestling, and its famous Kolhapuri chappals, Kolhapuri cuisine (misal pav, Kolhapuri mutton) and Kolhapuri saaj jewellery. The Mahalakshmi Temple at Bhavani Mandap anchors the city as one of India's foremost Shakti pilgrimage centres.

travel.airport: Kolhapur Airport (Chhatrapati Rajaram Maharaj Airport, IATA: KLH, approx. 9 km; flights to Mumbai, Bengaluru and other cities; taxis and app cabs available).
travel.railway: Chhatrapati Shahu Maharaj Terminus (KOP), in the heart of Kolhapur (approx. 2 km from the temple; autos and taxis readily available), well connected to Mumbai, Pune, Bengaluru and Hyderabad.
travel.road: In the city centre at Bhavani Mandap, Mahadwar Road, Kolhapur 416012; on the NH-48 corridor, approx. 375-380 km from Mumbai via the Mumbai-Bengaluru highway.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather. Navratri (September-October) and Kirnotsav (Sun festival) are the most vibrant times, but expect very heavy crowds; weekday mornings are quietest.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Open daily approx. 4:00 AM to 10:30 PM (verify - some listings say 4:30 AM to 11:00 PM or 5:00 AM to 10:00 PM; the sanctum closes briefly during rituals). General darshan is free (Mukh Darshan and Sparsh Darshan queues, both free); sevas and abhisheks carry separate charges. Dress modestly; mobile phones and cameras are restricted inside.
